hero.title: Interfaces built to last.
hero.inspect: See how this page is built

fold.label: Unfold the fox into its crease pattern
fold.caption: The fox is what you see on screen: the interface. Unfold it and you get the folds that shape it, the architecture. "See how this page is built" opens any page here the same way.

work.heading: This site, measured.
work.intro: These numbers are measured each time the site is published, and all of its code is public, so you can check every claim on this page.

js.label: of JavaScript your browser runs for this page

axe.note: run with axe on every change

parts.note: each shows its code, design values and last change

changelog.heading: Changelog
changelog.intro: My career, written like a software changelog. Each major version is a step up in responsibility and takes the name of a Costa Rican volcano, a higher one each time.

profile.summary: My career as an elevation profile, from {from} to today: {releases}. I'm on version {version} now.

notes.heading: Precrease
notes.intro: Notes on how software gets designed and built, from architecture to working with AI. I write them in public and include what went wrong.
notes.empty: The first crease is being folded. It introduces who I am and what this blog will cover.

notFound.title: This page isn't on the map.
notFound.body: The link may be outdated or mistyped.
notFound.aside: I've taken a few wrong trails myself. This one leads back home.

changelogPage.title: Changelog
changelogPage.description: Pablo Madrigal's career as release notes, from base camp to Irazú.
changelogPage.intro: My career as release notes, newest first. Each major version takes the name of a Costa Rican volcano, a higher one each time. Choose a summit on the map to go to its release.

map.label: Map of the volcanoes behind each release
map.pin: v{major} {codename}, {elevation}, {years}. Go to its release notes.
map.caption: Costa Rica's Central Volcanic Range at real coordinates. Contour lines every 250 m; the route follows the releases in order.

portrait.alt: Pablo Madrigal, head and shoulders, in glasses and a striped shirt. A diagonal fold turns part of the photo into the same face drawn as contour lines.
portrait.caption: Interface · architecture

privacyPage.title: What this site knows about you.

inspector.intro: Hover a block · Click to pin · Esc to leave
inspector.nothingSelected: Hover or pick a layer to see where it comes from.

precrease.name: Precrease
precrease.description: Pablo Madrigal's notes on how software is designed and built, from architecture to AI, written for engineers and for anyone curious about how it works.
precrease.empty: The first post is on its way. Subscribe to hear when it's out.

map.title: Topic map
map.description: Every Precrease topic as a tree, with how many posts sit in each branch.
map.intro: Topics are organized like a tree. Open one to see the smaller topics inside it; each topic's page collects every post below it.

precrease.scheduled: Scheduled for {date}: only visible in development

search.label: Search Precrease
search.none: No posts match. Try fewer words or clear a filter.

subscribe.title: Subscribe
subscribe.description: Get new Precrease posts as they come out, with RSS.
subscribe.heading: Get new posts as they come out
subscribe.intro: You don't need an account to follow Precrease. The simplest way is RSS: a feed that a reader app checks for you, so new posts show up there on their own.

steps.reader: Open a feed reader. Feedly and Inoreader work in any browser; NetNewsWire is free on Mac and iPhone.
steps.add: Add this address as a new feed:
steps.done: New posts appear in your reader as soon as they're published.

subscribe.topics: Every topic has its own feed. Open a topic from the {map} and use its RSS feed link.
subscribe.email: Prefer email? A newsletter is coming once the site moves to its own domain.
